_meta.method: Hand-curated by analyzing domain definitions and sample questions; pending refinement via LLM-as-judge

axes.D: Decomposability — can be split into independent parallel sub-tasks
axes.V: Verifiability — answer can be deterministically/automatically checked
axes.K: Knowledge concentration — relies on narrow specialized domain knowledge
axes.S: Solution diversity — multiple valid solution paths exist

rationale.D: Single legal-text passage → single categorical label. Cannot be split into independent sub-tasks. Decomposing rarely helps because the legal interpretation is integrative.
rationale.V: Categorical labels (binary or short categories) → string match works. Some ambiguity in label boundary (e.g., Relevant vs Irrelevant edge cases) brings it below 1.0.
rationale.K: Privacy law, contract law, etc. require specific legal domain expertise (statutes, precedents, doctrine). Highest K of any domain we test.
rationale.S: Path to label is essentially unique: read text → categorize. Voting between agents adds little because they all run the same procedure.

legal.data_match: ✅ Both GPT-4o and Claude show monotonic decreasing curves (Legal data is clean enough to trust)

rationale.D: Clinical vignettes require integrative reasoning across symptoms, history, labs, demographics. Some sub-tasks possible (option-by-option ruling out, differential diagnosis listing) but core reasoning is unitary.
rationale.V: 4-option MCQ with single correct answer letter → deterministic match. Slight imperfection because some questions have multiple defensible answers per medical literature.
rationale.K: Heavy USMLE-style medical knowledge: pathophysiology, pharmacology, clinical guidelines.
rationale.S: Differential diagnosis offers some diversity — multiple valid reasoning paths can converge on same answer letter.

medical.data_match: ⚠️ GPT-4o data flat (28.5%→25.8%); Claude shows increasing but 1-agent has only n=150 (insufficient). Need re-experiment.

code.task_type: free_form (function body generation, validated by unit tests)

rationale.D: Functions can be decomposed into helper functions; multiple agents can specialize in (1) signature understanding, (2) algorithm choice, (3) edge case handling, (4) test case generation. Most decomposable of all 5.
rationale.V: Unit tests give exact pass/fail. Highest V (=1.0) of all domains — only domain with execution-based verification.
rationale.K: Programming patterns are broad but each problem doesn't require very deep narrow knowledge. Mostly algorithmic + Python idioms.
rationale.S: Multiple valid algorithms typically exist (sort-based, scan-based, etc.). Voting/consensus among agents can identify failures.

code.data_match: ❌ Current data contaminated by empty-pred matching bug. Re-experiment required (T1.0 in EXPERIMENTS_NEEDED.md).

rationale.D: Argument structure can sometimes be decomposed (premise-by-premise validity check) but conclusions are often integrative. Mid-range D.
rationale.V: 4-option MCQ → deterministic match. Slight imperfection in fallacy categorization.
rationale.K: Formal logic and philosophical reasoning are taught in undergraduate philosophy — moderately specialized but not as narrow as medicine/law.
rationale.S: Multiple inferential paths can lead to same answer (direct vs by elimination).

logic.data_match: ⚠️ Claude shows weak inverted-U (peak at 2-agent: 22.27%); GPT-4o noisier especially with 4-agent partial data.

long_context.task_type: MCQ-4 over long passages (avg 22,500 chars context)

rationale.D: Long passages can be split between agents (e.g., one reads first half, another second half, then synthesize). Decomposability is genuinely useful here.
rationale.K: Answer is in the provided passage; minimal external knowledge required. Lowest K of all domains.
rationale.S: Multiple textual cues can support same answer; voting among agents reading same passage gives moderate diversity.

long_context.data_match: ✅ Claude shows strong 2-peak (3.33% → 19.73% → 7.43% → 1.55%). Trust pending truncation impact verification.
